Native crossmap

Objective: map the universal (nativedb) hash to this build's handler without using ScriptHookV's data.

Pipeline

Step Tool Output
Dump the image (game running, after initialisation) tools/dump/openv-dump.exe GTA5_Enhanced.exe out.bin research/dumps/<build>-a.bin
Walk the live registration table tools/dump/openv-natives.exe 3ED4C20 out.tsv current hash to handler (6748)
Recover registration order research/regorder.py <dump> 920d50 out.json 6671 natives in source order
Extract handler signatures research/features.py <tsv> out.json (uses trace.py) argument count and return kind per handler
Align research/solve.py <tsv> <features> out.json --order <regorder> (--holdout 0.2 to self-test) crossmap
Merge fallback research/merge.py reg.json addr.json final.json fills gaps from the handler-address pass
In-game check tools/probe/inject.exe openv-probe.dll research/probe.log

Key finding: the registration spine

Arxan scatters the registration code, but its execution order is intact:

  • A run of call 0x140920d50 instructions in the main .text, one per native, spaced 0x16 bytes apart, forms a spine.
  • Each call is entered from a scattered chunk: lea rdx,[handler]; movabs rcx,<hash>; jmp spine_i.
  • Sorting the spine by address yields source and registration order. That order matches nativedb order in 235 of 236 anchor steps.
  • It also covers natives whose handlers were merged by identical-code folding, which address order cannot place.

The functions at 0x140920d50 and 0x140920d70 both insert into the same table.

Handler signatures

research/trace.py follows Arxan jump chains:

  • direct jmp;
  • push r; lea r,[X]; xchg [rsp],r; ret;
  • ... lea rsp,[rsp+8]; jmp [rsp-8];
  • calls used as jumps;
  • context spilled to rsp or rbp slots.

It recovers the argument count for 93 percent of anchors and the return kind for 99 percent.

Accuracy

  • Holdout: 20 percent of anchors hidden and then recovered. The registration-order solve returns 46 of 47 exact, 0 wrong and 1 unmapped.
  • In game (story mode, 30 October 2026): 31 checks through openv-probe.dll, all passing, with no faults. Coverage included:
    • pure math and string natives;
    • platform flags;
    • timers;
    • PLAYER_ID, PLAYER_PED_ID and a GET_PLAYER_PED cross-check;
    • entity health, model and coordinates (Michael at his house);
    • GET_PLAYER_NAME.
  • Known incorrect: GET_CURRENT_LANGUAGE and LOCALIZATION_GET_SYSTEM_DATE_TYPE.
    • The game registers two natives in that slot that appear to be newer DLC natives absent from nativedb.
    • One takes a pointer argument and returns a bool; the other returns a bool.
    • Lesson: at namespace boundaries, natives unknown to nativedb displace the alignment. A common signature (zero arguments, integer return) is not evidence on its own.

Confidence tiers (in the crossmap JSON)

Tier Meaning
anchor Hash identical to the universal hash
solid Features match and the entry is aligned inside a segment where both sides have equal counts with every entry paired
high Features match strongly, but the alignment had gaps nearby
medium, low Weaker feature agreement

OpenV should load the anchor and solid tiers by default. For the other tiers it should verify the handler signature at runtime and log any mismatch when a script first calls that native.

Open items

  • Natives present in the game but absent from nativedb (approximately 50): detect them as unpaired game entries and exclude them from the alignment.
  • Script context: some natives read the current script thread from TLS (gs:[0x58], for example TIMERA). The probe avoided them; the real hook must run scripts inside a game script thread (Phase 2).
  • Patch day: rerun the pipeline. Anchors from the previous build's crossmap (old current hash to new current hash where the handler code is identical) should provide thousands of additional anchors.
